content.thinking:
Under the Act, tenants must give two months' written notice, so the one-month notice given is invalid. Since notice was given 10 Oct 2026, the earliest valid departure date would be two months later, around 10 Dec 2026, with no need to align with a specific rent period under the new rules.

Shortening that could only happen if the landlord agrees in writing to an early surrender—I should flag this as the landlord's decision rather than promise anything to the tenant. I also need to clarify that the deposit will be returned via the scheme after checkout within 10 days of agreement, that keys shouldn't be handed in yet since the tenancy continues, and that rent remains payable until the tenancy ends. I'll reply to the tenant with this guidance and separately request landlord approval regarding any early surrender.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. Since 1 May 2026 the notice a tenant must give is 2 months in writing, so one month's notice unfortunately can't end the tenancy on 10 November. Counting from your email today (10 October), the earliest end date is 10 December 2026. Rent stays due up to the end date.

If you need to leave sooner, your landlord can agree a shorter period in writing. We're asking him now and will come back to you. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you hear from us in writing. If you'd like, you can also confirm in writing that you want 10 December as your end date.

Keys: please hold on to them for now and don't drop them off yet. We'll confirm the handover date and place once the end date is settled.

Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. After the tenancy ends and keys are returned, we do a check-out and agree any deductions with you, then return the rest. We can't give you a date until then.

Thanks,
Mare & Co Lettings

arguments.decision_needed: Tenant Tom Achterberg (Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road) gave only 1 month's notice on 10 Oct 2026 to leave 10 Nov. Valid notice needs 2 months, so earliest end is 10 Dec 2026. Do you agree in writing to an earlier end date of 10 Nov?
options: Hold to 10 December 2026 (legal default, recommended unless you have a new tenant lined up)
Agree in writing to an earlier end date of 10 November 2026 (surrender by agreement)
Agree another date between 10 Nov and 10 Dec

Under the Act, tenants must give two months' written notice, so the one-month notice given is invalid. Since notice was given 10 Oct 2026, the earliest valid departure date would be two months later, around 10 Dec 2026, with no need to align with a specific rent period under the new rules.

Shortening that could only happen if the landlord agrees in writing to an early surrender—I should flag this as the landlord's decision rather than promise anything to the tenant. I also need to clarify that the deposit will be returned via the scheme after checkout within 10 days of agreement, that keys shouldn't be handed in yet since the tenancy continues, and that rent remains payable until the tenancy ends. arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. Since 1 May 2026 the notice a tenant must give is 2 months in writing, so one month's notice unfortunately can't end the tenancy on 10 November. Counting from your email today (10 October), the earliest end date is 10 December 2026. Rent stays due up to the end date.

If you need to leave sooner, your landlord can agree a shorter period in writing. We're asking him now and will come back to you. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you hear from us in writing. If you'd like, you can also confirm in writing that you want 10 December as your end date.

Keys: please hold on to them for now and don't drop them off yet. We'll confirm the handover date and place once the end date is settled.

Deposit: it's protected with mydeposits. After the tenancy ends and keys are returned, we do a check-out and agree any deductions with you, then return the rest. We can't give you a date until then.

Thanks,
Mare & Co Lettings
